name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  fmt:
    name: Format check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - name: cargo fmt --check
        run: cargo fmt --all --check

  file-size:
    name: File size cap (500 lines)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Lint only — CLAUDE.md's file-size rule and constraints.md R5 (BLOCKING).
      # AGENTS.md permits CI for "build, lint, typecheck, formatting and
      # packaging"; this is a lint, not a test.
      - name: Enforce the 500-line cap
        run: bash scripts/check-file-size.sh

  clippy:
    name: Clippy (pedantic)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - name: Install protoc
        uses: arduino/setup-protoc@v3
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Restriction gate (unwrap_used / expect_used, denied in
      # [workspace.lints.clippy]) runs on PRODUCTION code only — lib + bins.
      # Test/#[cfg(test)] code may use unwrap()/expect() (clippy.toml +
      # allow-in-tests). Both feature configs are checked so the dev-endpoints
      # auth-bypass path is also linted.
      - name: cargo clippy (production — restriction gate)
        run: |
          cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic
          cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins --features frf-gateway/dev-endpoints -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic
      # Test targets: pedantic only (unwrap/expect allowed per clippy.toml).
      - name: cargo clippy (tests — pedantic)
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic

  test:
    name: Test suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Install protoc
        uses: arduino/setup-protoc@v3
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --all

  msrv:
    name: MSRV check (Rust 1.85)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: "1.85"
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: Install protoc
        uses: arduino/setup-protoc@v3
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: cargo check (MSRV)
        run: cargo check --all

# RA11c cold snapshot order repair

Result: **Passed** for the ordered fold, current-source mounted behavior, and
cleanup. Production adoption remains **Blocked** by the fixed browser RSS gate.

The cold FRF fold now consumes each Electric message in response order. A delete
removes its key immediately; only a later insert recreates the row. An update merges
an existing row and rejects a missing row, matching Electric's documented operation
contract. The focused cases cover delete-then-reinsert, insert-update-delete, and
delete-then-update in one response.

Observed verification:

- `pnpm --dir web exec vitest run src/shared/sync/frf-shape-transport.test.ts`
  passed 22 tests.
- Controlled mutations restored the prior delete-last fold and separately removed
  the missing-update guard. Both selected tests exited 1. The repaired file was
  restored to SHA-256
  `4b42dd0db8771d3085a1ee3eb82daa0b510257b9beff0a72d1fbd116d4b2d14b`, and the
  complete 22-test file then passed.
- `pnpm --dir web typecheck` exited 0.
- `pnpm --dir web lint` exited 0 with no warnings.
- `python3 scripts/test-ra11c-materialization.py --timeout-seconds 180` ran the
  current source through real Postgres, Kratos, Gate/FRF, PGlite, and PEM. Both
  durable processes exited 0, all 11 behavior checks are true, and all five cleanup
  checks Passed.
- The mounted memory phase measured 1,008,877,568 incremental RSS bytes against
  536,870,912 allowed and 76,166,312 incremental heap bytes against 268,435,456
  allowed. RSS Failed; heap Passed. This completes the measurement and prohibits
  production adoption.

An isolated reviewer proposed returning `newer-generation` when a reopened schema
plan carries a generation below the persisted replica generation. The attempted
guard passed its nine ledger tests and an effective selected negative control, but
the mounted continuation then failed before reopening durable SQL. That process
intentionally reuses the base schema plan after refetch has advanced the persisted
generation. The guard was reverted; the existing exclusive-owner path preserves
the higher generation with `Math.max`, and the final mounted continuation passed.
The failed experimental run is retained in
`task-10-mounted-replay-final-after-ledger.log`.

The final security review found that 401/403 response bodies entered the
client-visible session-revocation reason. The transport now maps those statuses to
fixed messages without consuming the upstream body. Both status cases assert the
exact safe message and `bodyUsed === false`; a controlled mutation that published
the body made the selected 401 test fail. The final focused set passed 55 tests.

The prior aggregate focused runs remain Build-only because different PGlite tests
timed out on different attempts. No failed assertion was observed in those runs;
they are not reported as Passed.

ASO PostgreSQL and Kratos remain the authorities. Session denial is keyed by deployment,
Kratos issuer and verified Kratos session ID. Membership/capability authority is keyed by
deployment, ASO incarnation and monotonic global revision. ASO commits the revision and durable
outbox event in the same transaction and commits logout denial plus retry intent before asking
Kratos to revoke. Gate consumes this stream into a shared Redis coherency fence, disables L1/L2
use on lag, loss or regression, and still performs a fresh ASO authority-fence decision for every
protected authorization.

FRF holds the resulting grant through a shell-neutral protected-body lease. The Axum adapter
must yield frames from that lease instead of authorizing a completed buffered body. Active bodies
revalidate at most every 750 ms, bound the ASO authority RPC at 750 ms and propagate cancellation
within 250 ms. Authority timeout, loss or a changed session/grant tuple ends delivery and releases
continuation state. The gateway samples monotonic time before sub-second Unix time and passes both
to FRF. FRF anchors the grant deadline to that earlier monotonic sample and the exact integer JWT
expiry boundary, so dispatch delay cannot extend the grant. The response stream checks that
deadline before and after polling its receiver, preventing a queued frame from winning a scheduler
race with the background cancellation owner. A cancelled producer yields no later protected frame.

The 5,000 ms measurement starts at the authoritative ASO membership commit, durable session-denial
commit or verified expiry instant. It ends at the final protected frame produced by the server or
cancellation that prevents the next frame, followed by denial of a subsequent protected request.
For a revocation initiated directly in Kratos, the observable interval starts when a mounted path
holding the previously verified session first sees it inactive and commits the corresponding ASO
denial. Kernel/proxy buffers, network transit and client receipt are outside this server-controlled
claim; already produced bytes cannot be recalled.

# RA11c task 2.2 — crash recovery and replacement

Result: **Passed** for the scoped behavioral outcome.

Command:

`pnpm --dir web exec tsc --noEmit && python3 scripts/test-ra11c-materialization.py --timeout-seconds 180 --data-dir .runtime/ra11a-data/ra11c-materialization-acceptance`

Prerequisites were available locally: PostgreSQL, Kratos, Flint Gate, Flint
Realtime Fabric, Electric, the pinned PGlite package and the adopted PEM
package. The run used isolated durable PGlite storage and synthetic records.

The durable initial and continuation processes each exited 0. The observed
recovery sequence was:

1. The production materializer received the complete 16,203-row related
   snapshot. Its checkpoint write threw the named synthetic crash.
2. The transaction rolled back all five SQL tables and left the durable
   checkpoint null. PEM published no entity map or ordered list.
3. A normal cold sync then committed the complete snapshot and its five
   independent shape checkpoints.
4. A later case update was interrupted before checkpoint commit. Both the row
   and checkpoint retained their old values.
5. The update then committed to real PGlite SQL and its checkpoint while a
   synthetic process death prevented PEM publication. A new process reopened
   that durable state, obtained an authorized FRF response, and only then
   rebuilt the empty graph from committed SQL; `restartResumedWithoutSkip` was
   `true`.
6. Deleting a citation upstream forced a refetch generation. The replacement
   removed that row from SQL, its PEM entity, and its ordered list;
   `deleteForcedReplacement` was `true`.

The machine receipt records `coldCrashLeftNoPartialBatch`,
`crashRolledBackRowAndCheckpoint`, `restartResumedWithoutSkip`, and
`deleteForcedReplacement` as `true`. Cleanup returned `Passed` for every
resource. The authoritative receipt is `task-4-mounted-acceptance.json`.

The separate memory phase exited 1 because the fixed browser RSS gate failed;
that does not change this crash/refetch result and still blocks RA11c production
adoption.

# RA11c task 2.3 — authority event and owner fence

Result: **Passed** for the scoped behavioral outcome.

Commands:

`pnpm --dir web exec vitest run src/app/providers/session-access-boundary.test.tsx -t "fences protected content synchronously after replica revalidation fails"`

`python3 scripts/test-ra11c-materialization.py --timeout-seconds 180 --data-dir .runtime/ra11a-data/ra11c-materialization-acceptance`

Prerequisites were available locally: PostgreSQL, Kratos, Flint Gate, Flint
Realtime Fabric, Electric, the pinned PGlite package and the adopted PEM
package. The mounted run used isolated synthetic records and durable storage.

The React/Zustand boundary test passed 1 selected test: publishing a replica
revalidation failure removed protected content synchronously and rendered the
locked fallback in the same update.

The durable mounted phases each exited 0 and observed both runtime races:

- The worker owner was disposed after its request started. Its abort completed,
  the pending row stayed unchanged in SQL, its prior checkpoint stayed durable,
  and a replacement owner later applied the update.
- The real materializer received another case revision and passed its first
  five authority checks. The sixth check threw
  `ReplicaAuthorityFailure` after SQL work began but before checkpoint commit.
  The shared RA06 event subscriber synchronously received exactly
  `Replica grant changed during materialization.` The transaction rolled back,
  the checkpoint stayed unchanged, and PEM retained the prior Case entity.

The machine receipt records `disposedOwnerFencedPendingRevision`,
`replacementOwnerAppliedPendingRevision`, and
`authorityFailureEventPublishedAndFenced` as `true`. All five cleanup checks
returned `Passed`. The authoritative mounted receipt is
`task-4-mounted-acceptance.json`.

The restart campaign also forced a real PGlite process boundary after the SQL
row and complete checkpoint committed but before PEM publication. The next
process observed the durable row while its graph was empty, received an
authorized FRF response, and only then rebuilt the graph from committed SQL.
`restartResumedWithoutSkip` records that ordered recovery as `true`.

The separate memory phase still exits 1 at the fixed browser RSS gate. That
does not change this authority-fence result and continues to block production
adoption of the RA11c candidate.
